# Generated File Policy

Two files in this repo are regenerated by tooling rather than hand-edited,
and both were previously showing up as routine "dirty" diffs unrelated to
any real source change — this doc is the policy for both, so the pattern
doesn't quietly reappear elsewhere.

## `next-env.d.ts` — untracked

**Policy: not tracked.** Next.js regenerates it automatically on the next
`next dev` / `next build` / `next lint` run if it's missing — it's pure
TypeScript reference-directive boilerplate, never hand-edited (it says so
in its own header), and it churns on its own: dev mode and build mode point
at different `.next/types` paths, so the file's content differs between
"someone ran `npm run dev`" and "someone ran `npm run build`" with zero
actual code change.

- Untracked via `git rm --cached next-env.d.ts` + a `.gitignore` entry.
- If your local copy is missing (fresh clone), run `npm run dev` or
  `npm run typecheck` once — Next.js recreates it.
- Do not re-add it to git. If you see it as untracked in `git status`,
  that's correct — leave it alone.

## `public/sw.js` — tracked, but its `CACHE_VERSION` is Vercel-only

**Policy: tracked with a stable source placeholder.**
`scripts/stamp-sw.mjs` (run from `prebuild`) rewrites the file's
`CACHE_VERSION` constant to `golfhelm-v<commit-sha>` for real cache-busting
— but it now **only does this when `process.env.VERCEL` is set**, i.e. on
an actual Vercel build. A local `npm run build` (sanity-checking a
production build on a dev machine) or CI's `next build` gate no longer
touch the file at all.

Why: before this fix, *any* `npm run build` invocation rewrote the tracked
`public/sw.js` with a fresh hash/timestamp, which is why `git blame` on
that file shows a stray commit of a locally-stamped value
(`golfhelm-v48d739cec`) that was never a real deploy — someone ran a local
build, saw the file as modified, and committed it by habit. That's the
"routine hash churn as a commit-worthy diff" this policy closes.

- The tracked value is the literal placeholder `golfhelm-vsource` —
  recognizable at a glance as "not a real build stamp," never a
  commit-sha-shaped string.
- **Never hand-edit `CACHE_VERSION` to a hash.** If you need to force
  clients to bust their service-worker cache outside of a normal deploy,
  bump the placeholder string itself (e.g. `golfhelm-vsource2`) as a
  real, intentional, reviewable source change — not a stamped hash.
- Vercel's build environment always sets `VERCEL=1` and
  `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`, so real deploys still get a genuine
  per-commit cache-busting version; nothing about the actual
  cache-invalidation behavior changed.

## If you're about to add a new generated file to this list

Ask first: does it need to be tracked at all (could `.gitignore` + a "regen
if missing" step work, like `next-env.d.ts`), or does it need a stable
placeholder that's only rewritten in the one context that actually needs
the rewrite (like `public/sw.js`)? Either is fine — an untracked file that
routinely shows up as a dirty diff in `git status` on every build is not.
